column1: # Proposed memory bench floors (BENCH_SPEC section 12, BT20). A PROPOSAL, not a gate:
# nothing reads this file to fail a build yet. The informative CI job
# so a reviewer can see a row move before it is ever enforced.
# Policy, as for retrieval-baseline.tsv and coverage-floors.tsv:
# - bound `floor`: the value may rise freely; lowering it is a reviewed change that says why.
# - bound `ceiling` (false_*, stale_*, future_*, distractor_*, scale_exponent_*): the value may
#   fall freely; raising it is the reviewed change.
# - Refresh deliberately, from a baseline run, never to make a red run green.
# Source of the synth rows: the release build of branch feat/recall-bench at 64957773 (base
# variants/baseline.toml on 2026-09-26: quick-a strata, synth-v1 seed 7, mono, 10^3 entries,
# 4 questions per type (88 questions; A/A deltas 0, handles normalized). Smoke-sized: with
# n = 4 per type a single question moves a rate by 0.25 (BENCH_SPEC 11), so per-type rows are
# guards with margin 0 against a regression, never evidence of an improvement.
# Source of the scale rows: build times of the cached synth-v1 seed 7 mono stores at
# 10^3, 10^4 and 10^5 (batch 5000, same binary), least-squares slope of log10(ms) on
# log10(entries). Ask-latency exponents are not proposed yet: they need `full` at 10^4 on
# the latency cores, which has not run on this binary.
# The judged corpora keep their own recorded files (retrieval-baseline.tsv,
# jev-baseline.tsv, relate-baseline.tsv); their false_unknown and false_answer rows are
# repeated here only so the proposal is complete, with those files as the authority.
# B-real rows are a local release gate and stay outside the repository (privacy).
